def is_nested(string):
    '''
    Create a function that takes a string as input which contains only square brackets.
    The function should return True if and only if there is a valid subsequence of brackets 
    where at least one bracket in the subsequence is nested.

    is_nested('[[]]') ➞ True
    is_nested('[]]]]]]][[[[[]') ➞ False
    is_nested('[][]') ➞ False
    is_nested('[]') ➞ False
    is_nested('[[][]]') ➞ True
    is_nested('[[]][[') ➞ True
    '''
    # Check whether the string contains the contiguous substring '[[' followed later by ']]'
    first_open_index = string.find('[[')
    if first_open_index == -1:
        return False
    last_close_index = string.rfind(']]')
    if last_close_index == -1:
        return False
    return first_open_index < last_close_index
